results.quantity: Q3b: kinematic test: outflow vs disk/warp/tidal feature at Soutflow
results.value: PV diagrams (out/q3b/q3b_pv.png, kin_ns_cuts.csv, kin_ew_cuts.csv). (1) The "sharp red edge" is NOT diagnostic: the 25%-of-peak red edge is 2867-2872 km/s at Soutflow, 2867-2889 at S and 2832-2889 along the N-S cut at x=-0.2": the lobe has no gas redder than the S disk red edge, i.e. it is one-sided (blue only), not specifically cut at Vsys+100. (2) E-W rotation gradient at the S declination 35 km/s/arcsec (v0=2795): expected line sigma for disk gas on the minor axis from beam smearing ~62 km/s, observed 130-150 (HCN) / 112-135 (HCO+) at Soutflow vs 24 at the W control (-4.4,-4.5) and 49-104 at the mirror N of S: the broadening is not rotation smearing. (3) HCO+/HCN peak velocity at Soutflow is 2806-2814, i.e. at the disk systemic velocity (narrow component, sigma 32), plus a broad blue-only skirt: centroid offset -125 km/s relative to the rotation-curve value (2769-2789); the skirt grows with distance from S (N-S centroid 2754 at -2.7", 2629 at -4.5", edge of emission ~-5.9"). (4) No blue tail at the mirror position N of S (blue half HCN 0.027+-0.006 vs 0.215+-0.010 Jy/beam km/s at Soutflow) nor at the W control, E control empty. (5) At 0.5" (Xb4b) the S-lobe pixel velocities scatter by 113 (HCO+)-262 (HCN) km/s rms with only a weak N-S gradient (+44+-5 / +27+-2 km/s/arcsec, r=0.15-0.21; E-W gradient -28..+15), i.e. clumps with up to ~100-250 km/s relative motions on <100 pc, not a smooth gradient (disk gradients here <~45 km/s/arcsec). Which predictions: a smooth warp/tidal arm predicts line widths set by the beam-smeared gradient (~60 km/s), velocities continuous with the E-W curve, and symmetric red/blue clumps; the data show one-sided broad blue gas with sigma 100-150 km/s, centroid shifted -100..-250 km/s and clump-to-clump scatter >100 km/s, which prefers an outflow/entrained or strongly perturbed gas. Not rejected: a tilted-ring warp with a PA twist and v_rot~250 km/s could project -100..-300 km/s on the minor axis, and a tidal feature. Classification stays MEDIUM: more consistent with the dense-gas blue lobe of the S outflow (position/direction match Sakamoto+2014 and Michiyama+2018) than an isolated cloud, but disk-warp/tidal origin is an unrejected alternative.

results.quantity: Q4c: Q4 summary: origin of the factor-2 lower HCN/HCO+ 3-2 at S (final, differential)
results.value: SUPPORTED (low-medium confidence; 1-4 dof): (1) The contrast is only partly J-dependent: N/S = 1.49 at J=1-0 vs 1.9-2.0 at 3-2 (1.7"), so ~60% (log) of it is J-independent. (2) Joint RADEX fits including the 1-0 data prefer both lines thick with HCN more sub-thermal than HCO+ (class A: Tex 7 vs 11 K, HCN tau32 >~10; or separate densities F2, indistinguishable), and reject thin-HCN/abundance-only classes (C, D; Delta chi2 >= 64 (physT30; >= 28 for the grid prior)), independently of the Band-5 2-1 ratios; class B (different filling at equal Tex) fails the independent 1-0 prediction (0.43 vs 0.645). HCN tau32 > ~2 (95%), no upper limit. (3) Between N and S the data need a change of the HCN (or HCO+) column ratio by a factor 1.8-3 (logN(HCN) -0.25 to -0.5 dex), not of n or Tkin (Delta chi2 29-63 worse) and not only of filling (Delta chi2 8 worse). (4) CS/low-J data weakly favour an HCN (N-bearing) deficit over an HCO+ enhancement (HCO+/CS equal at N and S; HCN/CS and HNC/HCO+ lower at S) but CS 7-6 modelling is undecided (0.2-2.8 sigma). (5) IR pumping: no HCN v2=1f above alpha 0.03-0.09 (Tvib < 290-430 K), which does not exclude CON-like Tvib 200-300 K. (6) Shocks: SO (central 9x6" beam only) Trot < 12-25 K if equally extended, not excluded for compact warm gas; CH3OH is extended/off-nuclear (nuclei <0.013/<0.017 at 0.95"). NOT decided: excitation (A) vs separate densities (F2), HCN opacity upper range, abundance vs optical depth, HCO+ enhancement vs HCN deficit (tentative HCN deficit), whether N (poorly fitted, chi2 19-23/8) is a valid calibration. TENSION: with X(HCN)=1e-8 the HCN column implies Sigma 2e4-1e5 Msun/pc2, 4-20x above the CO maximum (5500); needs X(HCN) >~ 2e-7 or a clumped geometry the one-zone RADEX does not describe. Centroids (HCN minus HCO+ per 40 km/s bin, r<1.2", Xb4d): dx = +0.04..+0.06" (blue), -0.001 (0), -0.09 (+80), -0.125+-0.034" (+120 km/s); Xb4b 0.30": +0.02 -> -0.038+-0.003" (+80); dy <=0.04": HCN emission is systematically closer to the nucleus than HCO+ at every velocity (HCO+ centroid moves -0.5" -> +0.28" across the line), with a larger offset on the red side, consistent with an HCN-richer compact core mixed in a 1.05" beam with lower-ratio extended gas

(1) With 7 independent data the one-zone N fit is marginal only if the beam geometry is held fixed (profile chi2 9.1/3 dof, p=0.028); with the geometry (extended filling at 1.7", compact size) given the widths measured from the 0.25/0.95/1.7/5.7" Tb growth curve it is acceptable (chi2 3.2/3, p=0.36; 1.5-3.2, p=0.36-0.67 over the measured-geometry variants). (2) The Bayesian preference for two components at N (dlnZ(2cT-1z)=+3.0, fixed geometry) vanishes with measured geometry (-1.7), with the 25% error floor (+1.2) and with judgement geometry widths (-0.2 to +0.7); in simulations the +3 threshold is exceeded by 14.5% [10-20%] of data-consistent one-zone truths with wrong sizes, so it is not significant; with measured-geometry priors the statistic has no power to separate the truths (two-comp truths give dlnZ -1.0 to -1.2, one-zone truths -0.4 to -2.1). (3) S: one-zone adequate (chi2 5.2/3, p=0.16; measured geometry 3.1/3), dlnZ -0.8 to +0.4; Tkin 19-23 K (16-84% 14-35 K), Tbg<=5 K branch unchanged (20 K [14,32] at Tbg 5 K), P(T>=80 K)<=0.06. N compact Tkin is unconstrained (12-96 K; 62 [39,96] fixed-geometry one-zone, 15 [12,25] measured-geometry one-zone, 27 [14,70] two-comp). (4) Delta T = T_N - T_S is unconstrained: joint draw-by-draw over 16 deblend variants P(T_N>T_S)=0.47-0.60 with measured geometry (variant range 0.23-0.88), 0.72-0.93 at fixed geometry; Delta T median -0.5..+4 K [16-84%: -10, +36] with measured geometry, +10..+35 K at fixed geometry. interpretation:
Line inventory (corrected): besides HCN and HCO+ (J=2-1,3-2,4-3) and CS 7-6, CH3OH is detected (Band 5 165 GHz Q-branch J=1-3 at 27 sigma; 2(0)-1(-1) E at 254.015 GHz at 10 sigma), SO 5(4)-4(3) (Band 5, 8 sigma) is detected, HOC+ is tentative; everything else is a limit, blended or an edge artefact. CH3OH is cold/subthermal (Q-branch J>=4 and Eu>45 K lines absent; LTE Trot~9 K, but LTE and RADEX fits are poor) and extended: the Xb4d (0.9") CH3OH flux is only ~55% of the 9"-beam value, and in Xb4d it peaks on the Bridge and a W clump, not on the N and S nuclei (CH3OH/HCO+ 0.05 there vs <0.015 at the nuclei) - a shock/low-excitation tracer signature that agrees qualitatively with Harada+2018. The extended disk is defined (Xb55 HCO+ 2-1 S/N>5 at r>8", HCN/HCO+(2-1)=0.51) but is not detected in the 3-2/4-3 data with the available sensitivity/zero-level. The southern blue-shifted component 1.9" south of S is statistically solid (7-12 sigma after null calibration, 0 null peaks above 8 sigma in 583 beams), has no red counterpart, is not a PSF-sidelobe copy of S, and has HCN/HCO+(3-2)~1.8 versus 0.4 at S; it is a separate broad component at ~2560-2650 km/s. The N and S nuclei are separable in Xb4b, Xb4d, Xb4f, Xb47 (not in Band 5). The opacity test (H13CN) can only give HCN/H13CN>7-9 (conditional on the CO-wing model). Raw HCN/HCO+ (3-2) peak ratios (N 0.6-1.0, S 0.4-0.5) are preliminary and not beam matched across OUS (Q1). Q1 (rev. 2): At matched 1.05" the northern nucleus has HCN/HCO+ 3-2 = 0.83+-0.04 and the southern (AGN) nucleus 0.40+-0.02 (N/S = 2.0-2.1, constant over the line core, insensitive to the velocity window to <=2.5% and to Xb4b vs Xb4d); the AGN has the lowest ratio, i.e. no HCN enhancement at the AGN (as Harada+2018). Blended 6.5"/10" aperture ratios hide this (N/S 1.1-1.2), but deblending the native-beam Band 7 4-3 map with the 1" templates recovers N/S = 1.9+-0.5 (N 0.47, S 0.25) and CS 7-6/HCO+ 3-2 is the same at N and S within errors (S/N 1.09+-0.48; HCN/CS 1.9x lower at S, 1.2 sigma: weak); at 2-1 (9" beam) the N-S pair is not separable (contrast 1-3, template-limited). The ladders (3-2/2-1, 4-3/3-2: HCN 0.35/0.39 (N), HCO+ 0.43/0.48) are strongly sub-thermal and the same at N and S within 14% (HCN 4-3/3-2 lower at S, 1.8 sigma): a quick RADEX grid gives n(H2) <~ 1e5 cm-3 and Tkin >~ 30 K at N, and requires N(HCN)/N(HCO+) >= 3 at both nuclei; since the ladders do not differ, the factor-2 N/S HCN/HCO+ contrast must come mainly from the HCN/HCO+ abundance (or HCN column/opacity) rather than density or temperature (equal-X disfavoured at ~2 sigma only). The disk 2-1 HCN/HCO+ is 0.47-0.50, 15-25% below the nuclei at the same beam; its 3-2 deficit is fully consistent with missing short spacings in Xb4f for a 13-14" scale structure (B_min = 8.7 m assumed), so no excitation difference of the disk can be claimed from HCO+; the HCN 3-2 deficit is larger than recovery alone explains but depends on the zero level. The Soutflow blue-wing HCN/HCO+ is 1.2-1.8 depending on estimator (candidate, single position, HCO+ wing 5-7 sigma). Resolution forces an 'active region versus disk' comparison at J=2-1 and for the disk, but not at J=3-2 and 4-3, where N and S are distinguishable. Q3 (outflow, revised): dense gas (HCN 12.6 sigma, HCO+ 5 sigma) is detected 1.9" (370 pc) S of the S nucleus at the blue lobe of the southern edge-on outflow (MEDIUM confidence; a disk warp/tidal feature is not rejected). In fixed a-priori apertures with velocity relative to the local centroid the blue-half HCN/HCO+ 3-2 ratio is 1.0-1.4, robustly above S (0.15-0.46) but not significantly different from N (1.13) and Bridge (1.3); the earlier 1.7 was peak-selected (+10% noise bias, rest spatial gradient); the whole broad component has 0.72-0.8 (N-like). Blends (CH3NH2, CH2NH, CH3CHO, CH3SH, CH3OH) are limited to <=10-18% of the HCN blue side by LTE fits to other lines; HDO untestable. No dense-gas wing at N: 3 sigma <2-4% (HCN, blue 225-750 km/s) of core, mass <=1.3e6-1.4e7 Msun; weak 2-3 sigma hints at North-OF-Blue are not significant. Soutflow dense mass 1.4-6.5e6 Msun (alpha 3-10), ~6-37% of the S-outflow CO high-velocity mass depending on X20. Q4 (final): the J=1-0 literature data (Harada+2018 Table 13, 1.7 arcsec: HCN/HCO+ N 0.96, S 0.645) show that ~60% (in log) of the N/S contrast of the 3-2 ratio (1.9-2.0) is already present at 1-0 (1.49): the contrast is mostly J-independent, not excitation. Joint RADEX fits (including 1-0, a separate-density class, BIC/marginal likelihood) prefer both lines thick with HCN more subthermal than HCO+ (Tex ~7 vs ~11 K; HCN tau32 >~2, >~10 for common n; A and separate-n F2 indistinguishable) and reject thin-HCN/abundance-only classes (Delta chi2>=65), also without the Band-5 2-1 ratios; different filling at equal Tex (B) fails the independent 1-0 prediction. Between N and S the data require the HCN (or HCO+) column ratio to change by 1.8-3x, not n or Tkin; N is poorly fitted by every one-zone model, and 8 data cannot constrain two-component models. CS and low-J ratios weakly favour an HCN deficit over an HCO+ enhancement (HCN/CS and HNC/HCO+ lower at S, HCO+/CS equal) but this is <=1.2 sigma in the data. Q9 (velocity-resolved ratios, revised after review): HCN/HCO+ 3-2 is NOT strictly flat in velocity, and the supported statements are: (i) at the N nucleus at 0.30" (r<0.25", 50 pc) the window-integrated ratio is 0.92-1.04 across +-100 km/s (~12% blue-to-red decline) and 1.05+-0.13 in the 100-260 km/s wings (no significant rise; core 0.98+-0.013); (ii) at 1.05" (r<0.5") there is a significant monotonic trend, +0.08+-0.006 per 100 km/s, with the wings (100-260 km/s stacked 1.19+-0.10, lower limit >1.2 at 150-250 km/s) 4 sigma above the core (0.77); the same trend appears when Xb4b is convolved to 1.05" (+0.072+-0.008) and vanishes at 0.30" (-0.003+-0.013), HCN centroids lie 0.04-0.13" closer to the nucleus than HCO+, and an injection of the measured radial ratio gradient with identical kinematics reproduces ~60-70% of the slope (+0.049): it is predominantly a beam/spatial-mixing effect with a residual (+0.02-0.03 per 100 km/s) not reproduced by the injection, which could be an HCN wing excess of a few 0.1 in the ratio from gas with a different ratio or lower HCO+ opacity; (iii) the S deficit is present at all velocities with HCN detected: 0.37-0.45 from the core to |v|~260 km/s (stacked wings 0.44+-0.03 at 1.05", 0.44+-0.05 at 0.30"), i.e. 2-3x below N, valid for |v|<~260 km/s where HCN is detected (HCO+-only beyond); (iv) the Bridge wing ratio rises to >=1 (1.35+-0.32 stacked 100-260 km/s vs core 0.44). Physically (RADEX with equal filling): the N core ratio ~1 with per-channel Tb(HCN)/Tb(HCO+)=0.96-0.97 over the full profile is what two optically thick (tau>~3), thermalised lines of the same Tex and width produce (ratio -> 1 for X<=3), with peak Tb of only 1.5-2.8 K implying filling factors 0.02-0.35; it does not constrain the abundance ratio X for X<=3. S (0.42) cannot be two thick equal-Tex lines: it needs lower N(HCN)/N(HCO+)<=1 with moderate HCN opacity, or Tex(HCN)<Tex(HCO+) at lower density; the fact that the S ratio is constant over the whole profile argues for a ratio set by the gas as a whole rather than by the line core saturating. An opacity-driven core dip is not seen anywhere. The 4-3/3-2 ladder (6.5") separates N and S only through Xb4d weights: R(4-3/3-2, Tb) is 0.46 (N) vs 0.30 (S) for HCN and 0.575 vs 0.40 for HCO+, and the red-wing HCO+ drop (0.50 -> 0.40) is mostly (~2/3) N/S weighting, since red HCO+ flux is 81% S.

Q2 (non-LTE ranges; credible intervals, not best fits; revised after the temperature-floor and Tbg tests): both nuclei are described by optically thick (tau32 HCN ~5-50), sub-thermal HCN and HCO+ (Tex 6-11 K, Tkin>>Tex) in gas of log n(H2)~4.5-5.5 (3e4-3e5 cm-3) with column degeneracies of ~0.5 dex. Density is not distinguishable between N and S. With no temperature floor S is Tkin ~15-50 K (T>=80 K excluded at >3 sigma) and N is 25-100 K (class dependent; a warmer N is only suggestive). The robust N/S difference is the excitation pattern: Tex(HCN)/Tex(HCO+)~0.86 at N vs 0.63 at S (the only both-thick solution that reproduces R32=0.39 and the 1-0 ratio), valid for a background Tbg<=5 K (continuum-based Tbg,eff 3.0-3.7 K); for Tbg>=10 K the equal-Tex solution is preferred at S. Bridge, disk, wing and outflow regions have only one or two ratios: R32 alone gives n>=1e5 cm-3 and no temperature constraint, and the single-molecule ladders are band-degenerate (T 10-150 K, 2.5-5 dex in n). Abundances: X(HCN) is not measured; the CO surface density demands X(HCN)>~1e-7 (Sigma_max 470 Msun/pc2) or >~1e-8 (Sigma 1e4) if the HCN column fills the beam. The H13CN limits and the velocity-resolved ratios do not add constraints; CS is class dependent. Q12 update (round 2, supersedes the earlier Q12 paragraph and the 'chi2 19-23/8' statistic): the fit statistic is the profile chi2 of 7 independent data (R32 removed; it equals R10*(H32/10)/(O32/10)), with Gaussian nuisance penalties, calibrated by simulation, plus the marginal likelihood for model comparison. A compact optically thick core plus envelope does not 'fix' the N one-zone fit in any testable sense: two-component models have as many effective parameters as data (8 vs 7) and chi2~0, and the one-zone N misfit (chi2 9.1/3, p=0.03 at fixed geometry) disappears (chi2 3.2/3, p=0.36) when the extended filling at 1.7" and the compact size take the widths measured from the 0.25/0.95/1.7/5.7" growth curve (N compact FWHM 0.44" [0.25-0.57], u=1.6 [1.1-3.0]). The evidence for two components at N (dlnZ=+3.0 at fixed geometry) is not significant (14.5% of data-consistent one-zone truths with wrong sizes exceed +3; 0% with right geometry) and turns to -1.7 with measured geometry, where the statistic has no power to tell one-zone from two-component truths. The H13CN limit removes 50-80% of the N two-comp posterior mass (compact tau32 median 23-37 -> 5-14); the claims n_c>1e6 and tau32 10-100 are prior-edge and geometry dependent. S needs no second component; Tkin 19-23 K (14-35 K), P(>=80 K)<=0.06 holds against geometry, floor, Tbg 5 K and H13CN. N compact Tkin is unconstrained (12-96 K); the N-vs-S contrast is not significant (joint over 16 deblend variants: P(T_N>T_S) 0.47-0.60 with measured geometry, 0.72-0.93 at fixed geometry). Confidence: N temperature low, S temperature medium-low, N-vs-S contrast low (unconstrained). A 1-0 map at matched ~1" resolution (only Harada+2018 1.7" 12m-only values are available) is the datum that would break the geometry degeneracy.
caveats: Peak-pixel intensities use different native beams per OUS; no cross-OUS ratio in this item is beam matched (Q1/Q6).

Systemic velocity 2780 km/s is a single adopted value; nuclear peak velocities differ by ~100 km/s at 0.25" (N 2811-2817, S 2710), so +-350 km/s windows are not centred on each nucleus; the HCN/HCO+ integrals use the same fixed window for both lines.

Line identifications rest on Splatalogue CDMS/JPL rest frequencies at v=2780 km/s; HOC+, SO 4_5-3_4 and both unidentified features need independent confirmation (e.g. matching J transitions at matched beam).
The Band-5 cubes do not separate N, S, Bridge (13% leakage at the nuclear separation, single HCO+ 2-1 peak pixel).
Empirical noise comes from emission-free pixels at 6-11" (primary-beam-corrected noise there is 1.2-1.6x the central value), which makes limits conservative by up to ~1.5x.
Xb4b nuclear emission is clumpy: peak-pixel values depend on the exact pixel chosen (search radius 1"); spectra are non-Gaussian (double-horned), Gaussian FWHM are indicative only.
No source of data for line-free-channel continuum from cubes exists (cubes are continuum-subtracted); the contamination check relies on mfs vs cont images, which have 1-2 sigma noise.
The 'aperture' (1.5" radius) rows of the line table use statistical noise only (no empirical null).
The conversion to K km/s uses the Rayleigh-Jeans formula with the beam of each cube; distance 40 Mpc is only used for pc sizes.

CH3OH LTE/RADEX fits have chi2/dof ~9-11: the numbers Trot=9 K and n>=1e7 are formal; the robust statement is 'Q-branch J>=4 absent: low excitation'. Baseline ripple of ~0.2 K km/s is visible in Band 5 (J=5 at -4 sigma).
Local-velocity matching (not 2780 km/s) is essential for identifications at S (2710-2740 km/s): at vsys the 251.66 feature would favour NS; at local velocity it clearly favours CH3OH.

The zero level of Xb4f/Xb55 moment-0 maps at r>8" is biased by about -0.5 / -1.3 Jy/b km/s (negative bowl, missing short spacings); disk fluxes are zero-level-corrected with the r=14-22" ring and carry >=0.3 Jy/b km/s systematic.

Soutflow position error is dominated by the assumed 10% beam pointing floor (0.10"), not by the fit (0.01-0.02"); wing definition relative to v_S=2722; comparison with the CO outflow geometry (Sakamoto+2014, Michiyama+2018) has not been made quantitatively.
H13CN limit conditional on the CO-wing family; log-quadratic/cubic wings can absorb a genuine H13CN signal.
Literature cross-check is from abstracts/summaries (Harada+2018, Sato+2022), not their tables.

Q1: ratio uncertainties are dominated by systematics (window truncation ~5%, absolute flux scale 10% per band); statistical errors are <=1% at the nuclei. Noise uses few line-free windows contaminated at times by weak lines (quietest quartile used), so faint-region limits are approximate.
Q1: regions use fixed nominal positions; the N ratio varies across its sub-clumps (IQR 0.05-0.09 at 1.05"), so a different aperture centre changes N by ~0.03-0.05.

Q1: the decline of HCN/HCO+ and the low 3-2/2-1, 4-3/3-2 ladder ratios at 10" mix Band 5, 6 and 7 data with different resolved-out fractions (Q6: Xb4f is the most complete Band 6 set); they should be treated as inputs to RADEX with 14% errors, not as evidence for a nuclear difference.

Q1: the Xb55 2-1 "disk" may include beam wings of the nuclei and NEclump; the ring zero level (-1.2 to -2.0 Jy/b km/s) is not present in line-free channels, so the sign of the correction is uncertain.

Q1b: the deblending assumes a uniform ratio inside each template component and that the 1" 3-2 template traces the same gas as the coarse line; chi2_r of the fits is 7-44 even with a 3% floor, so formal errors are meaningless and template systematics (a factor ~2 on N/S flux ratios at 2-1) dominate. Only the 4-3 N/S HCN/HCO+ contrast (1.9+-0.5) survives the injection test.

Q1b: the disk recovery model assumes B_min and a single Gaussian disk; the array identity is inferred from beam sizes (no uv information in the products). The zero-level (ring) correction of the disk maps changes the 3-2 ratio by a factor of 4, so disk 3-2 statements are limits.

Q1b: RADEX constraints come from 5 ratios and 4 parameters (1 dof), assume equal beam filling for all lines and a single (n, T) per region for HCN and HCO+; they bound n(H2) and X, not the absolute columns. The H13CN limit is conditional on the CO-wing model of p0001.

Q3 (round 2): outflow classification rests on kinematics (one-sided broad blue gas, mirror/control positions) and literature geometry, not CO; disk-warp/tidal origin unrejected. Blend limits cover CH3NH2, CH3OH, CH2NH, CH3CHO, CH3SH only (HDO and exotic species untested) and assume HCO+-like profiles. Xb4b (independent array) gives lower ratios (blue half 0.9-1.0 vs 1.2-1.4) and recovers ~55% of the flux: ratio systematics 10-25%. Noise is statistical (flux scale 5-10% common to all positions). The two-Gaussian split is shape-dependent (chi2/dof 2.6).
